name: Iowa-class battleship after the 1982 reactivation (USS New Jersey, BB-62)

published.source: en.wikipedia 'Iowa-class battleship': 887 ft 3 in overall, 108 ft 2 in beam, about 36 ft draught

references.name: [D1] Iowa class drawing, profile (1945 fit)
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Iowa classe battleships drawing.jpg' (profile and plan at one scale), 1600 x 589
references.note: Scaled on the published 270.4 m: stern col 23, stem head col 1572 (1549 px, 5.73 px/m). Waterline taken at row 294 (the drawn hull bottom amidships; it rises to row 290 at the bow, about 0.7 m, read as the drawing's trim or line weight). Only the hull and the 01 level (z 0.4..9.6) are compared: everything above is the 1945 fit (40 mm, ten 5-inch, the pole masts), which the 1980s ship does not carry. The stern crane (1945) is left out. One pixel is 0.17 m.

references.name: [D2] Iowa class drawing, plan (1945 fit)
references.note: Along the length 1551 px for 270.4 m (5.736 px/m), but across it the deck reads 200 px, 34.9 m against the published 32.97 m beam: 6 per cent wide (line weight and the 40 mm tub sponsons amidships), so it is kept for the plan taper and the stations only, not gated.

references.name: [P1] Missouri (BB-63) in dry dock, stern view (1980s)
references.source: DPLA / US Navy 'A stern view of the battleship USS MISSOURI (BB-63) as it lies in dry dock during a yard period'
references.note: For the reviewer only: the knuckle round the stern, the two skegs, the twin rudders and the four screws.

must_show: long fine hull 270.4 m, the deck plan at full beam from about x -40 to x 0 and narrowing to about 2 m at the stem x 135.2 (D2); the sheer rising from 7 m at x 55 to 13.2 m at the stem, the bulwark to about 14.1 m at x 134 (D1)
convex clipper stem raked about 6.7 m from the waterline to the deck (x 128.5..135.2) and the round cruiser stern at x -135.2 with its knuckle about 2.4 m under the deck edge (D1, P1)
three triple 16-inch turrets: No. 1 at x 57.0 (roof 11.3), No. 2 superfiring at x 36.4 (roof 14.3), No. 3 aft at x -65.3 facing aft (roof 11.7) (D1)

the tower foremast x -6.6..10.3 to 29.3 m, the upper tower to the director platform at 36.2 m and the Mk 38 director at x 7.6 with its Mk 13 antenna to about 41.4 m; the armoured conning tower ahead of it at x 24.6 (D1)
two stacks with black caps: the forward one at x -2.7 hard against the tower (cap 31 m), the after one at x -28.8 (cap about 29.7 m) (D1)

the 1980s fit: three twin 5-inch mounts a side (x 8.9, -0.6, -11.5), eight Mk 143 armored box launchers (x -17.4 on the 02 level, x -41.5 on the 01 level), four quad Harpoon canisters at x -36.2 and -39.4 beside the after stack, four Phalanx (x -2.2 on sponsons at 19.4 m, x -24.0) (1980s photographs, per the model's header)
the black lattice foremast over the tower top x -1.4..4.0, the SPS-49 at its head about 44 m and the pole topmast to 55 m (1980s photographs)
no crane on the fantail; the grey painted fantail with the white landing spot x -128..-73 (1983 overhead), teak deck elsewhere from x -134.6 to the stem

landmarks.name: No. 1 turret roof
landmarks.note: D1 col 1124, top row 229 (one pixel 0.17 m, so 0.25 m tolerance). The box keeps to the roof's port edge: No. 2's barrels overhang No. 1's roof at y 0 and +-3.05

landmarks.name: stem head bulwark
landmarks.note: D1 col 1566, top row 213; the drawn bottom rises 0.7 m toward the bow, hence 0.3 m

not_confirmed: everything above the 01 level is checked against no 1980s drawing: the only scaled drawing is the 1945 fit, and the 1980s photographs (port broadside 1983, overheads) could not be fetched for this spec (Commons API rate-limited, 2026-11-26); stations of the box launchers, Harpoons and Phalanx come from the model's earlier reading of them
the Mk 13 antenna's shape and its post: drawn as an upright curved strip 2.3 m across, its top matched to D1
the underwater body: skegs, screws and rudders from P1's proportions only; the outer shafts lie inside the hull's bilge (the gate's 0.5 m standing-off parts at x -96..-70)
the waterline: D1's drawn bottom rises 0.7 m toward the bow; the model is level
